newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica del Peru to invest $550-600 mln in '97.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica del Peru to invest $550-600 mln in '97.

text.p: Spanish-controlled Telefonica del Peru SA plans to invest $550 million to $600 million in 1997, down from $660 million in investment last year, its general manager said Tuesday.

"This year we plan to invest $550 million to $600 million, a figure roughly the same as last year," said Manuel Garcia, general manager of Telefonica del Peru, which is majority owned by Telefonica de Espana.

Garcia told a news conference that the investment figure is down slightly from 1996 because, after three years of infrastructure investments in Peru, Telefonica now has built up a stock of lines available for new customers.
"We now have a significant infrastructure of vacant lines," he said.

Telefonica de Espana bought control of Peru's two state- owned telecommunications firms in 1994 for $2 billion and merged them to create Telefonica del Peru and promised to invest another $1.9 billion until the end of 1999.
Between June 1994 and the end of 1996, Telefonica had invested some $1.5 billion, Garcia said.

Next year's investments will include $400 million in spending on installation of basic wire lines, between $70 million and $80 million on new cellular lines and the rest in other areas of the company, he said.
"As the years go by, investment will decrease because we already have infrastructure available," he added.
Telefonica de Espana also controls or operates telecommunications firms in Argentina, Chile and the Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul.
